steps.name: install --load: launchctl adapter closed over one label
criteria: --load on an unloaded job runs, in order, print gui/<uid>, print of the job, bootstrap, print again, and the output says 'harvest install: loaded gui/<uid>/<label>'; on a loaded job it boots out before it bootstraps; a second install --load reloads the same way
Both files are written before the first launchctl call; only print, bootstrap and bootout are ever called, only this session and this label, never kickstart

A session launchd does not offer, a failing bootstrap and a failing bootout each exit 1 install.launchctl-failed with the files left written and, after a bootout failure, no bootstrap attempted; re-running once launchd works finishes the job

steps.implementation_notes: Contract shape: bounded-change; universe = the one job gui/<uid>/<label>. createLaunchctl({ uid, label, plistPath }) closes over the label and plist path and returns a reader (print) and a controller (bootstrap, bootout); the capability cannot address any other job, so 'touched another label' is non-representable. Plain install still holds no launchctl at all; only --load wires the controller. Earned Trust: the controller probe runs print gui/<uid> first and a failure refuses install.launchctl-failed naming the domain; a loaded job is booted out before bootstrap because bootstrap of an already-loaded label is unconfirmed (the shim fails it with status 5, tagged @unconfirmed-behaviour); never rely on its behaviour. 'Loaded' is the exit status of print, not its text (pinned decision 12). Call sequence is pinned decision 8. Upstream Issue 1 ruling: when --load fails after the files were written the plan and per-file lines stay on stdout and the failure goes to stderr; the tests do not pin stdout there, so print nothing new. The adapter imports child_process and nothing from a sibling adapter. Enabling mechanism: per-scenario scenario( to it( as in 01-01; keep the red-gate import until step 10-01. The real launchctl is never reachable from a test: do not remove or bypass the bare-name and shim-first invariants.

steps.name: status: a read-only report of installed, loaded, drift and what would fail
criteria: status reports installed, schedule, loaded, state, runs, last exit code, drift 'none' and node 'ok' for a loaded job, plus state and pid for a running one (@unconfirmed-format); a failed last run, an unloaded job and nothing installed are each a report with exit 0
'Loaded' is the exit status of launchctl print, not its text; a print that fails for any reason reads as not loaded and status still exits 0
